questionText:
Read the following case study and answer the question:

"Dr. Arvind, an experienced clinical psychologist, conducted a diagnostic evaluation of Rohini, an 18-year-old student referred for chronic fatigue. In the opening stage, Dr. Arvind greeted Rohini warmly, explained the assessment purpose, established ground rules, and built rapport. In the substantive body of the interview, he utilized open-ended questions: 'Tell me about how your daily routine has changed over the past three months.' When Rohini hesitated, he employed probing prompts: 'Can you describe what you were feeling when you woke up this morning?' Importantly, Dr. Arvind avoided leading questions such as 'You feel depressed because of your parents' divorce, don't you?' He observed non-verbal cues: Rohini avoided eye contact, spoke in a slow monotone (paralanguage), and displayed slouched posture (kinesics).
